output.title: Design out the loop that feeds itself
output.body:
When a workflow keeps correcting its own mistakes, the last error is usually not the real problem. The problem is the loop that sends bad data back into the same process.

The bounded question to ask is simple: which repeated manual task creates the next round of rework? A common example is manual invoice entry that later has to be checked by hand because the first entry was incomplete or misclassified. That is the loop to design against.

Before you automate anything, check whether the workflow is actually a fit. Is it repetitive, does it produce a measurable outcome, and does it already live in digital documents or SaaS tools? If not, AI probably does not belong there. Change the process first.

If it does fit, define one error-blocking control before you build. That could be duplicate detection, mandatory field validation, or human approval before a high-risk step. For money movement, human approval stays mandatory.

Then scope one pilot around one workflow and one control. Not the whole business. Keep the build technical and the decision human. That is usually the cleanest way to break a self-reinforcing error loop.
